_README: THE WITHDRAWAL REGISTER. A retired figure or claim is DECLARED here, by id, and
`eval/tools/docstat.py --withdrawn` asserts that no LIVE document states it outside a
block that cites that id. Read `_check_withdrawal_register` in docstat.py for the rule
and for what it cannot see.
WHY DECLARED AND NOT INFERRED. The obvious alternative - a cross-document
figure-agreement check - was built and measured under task 11 and comes out against:
52 labelled figures over six live docs, 1 disagreement, and that one a false positive.
It cannot see a stale figure, because the restatements of a stale figure AGREE to the
digit. Propagation and consistency are the same observation (#113). What separates a
live figure from a retired one is not in the numbers; it is whether a withdrawal was
ever declared, which is a fact about the record and has to be written down.
APPEND-ONLY. An entry is never deleted and never edited to say something else. It is a
record of a decision that was made, and a consumer that applied it must keep being able
to. Add `reinstated` with a date and a reason if a withdrawal is itself reversed.
FIELDS
id           the exemption key. A live document may state the entry freely inside any
block that carries this string. Nothing else exempts anything - not a
file, not a line number, not a marker word.
match        every one of these regexes must occur inside one block for that block to
count as stating the entry. ALL, not any: a single loose pattern would
fire on unrelated prose.
anchor       an ARCHIVE file where the entry is stated in full and correctly. The
check proves its own extraction here before trusting it anywhere: an
entry that matches nothing in its anchor is reporting its own silence,
and is a failure, not a pass (AGENTS.md rule 12).
declared_in  where the withdrawal is argued, for a person.
replaced_by  what to state instead. A withdrawal with no replacement leaves the next
author with the same gap that produced the bad figure.

entries.claim: tier 3's separation result stated as 'between-stack range of mean ranks 1.70, mean gap 2.05'
entries.why: It named no population - no run, no game, no aspect set, no date - and reproduces under no method. The only field tier 3 has judged gives 1.900/2.275 pre-repair and 2.100/1.925 post-repair on rank/pool, and the quantity has two free method parameters, so there are four readings per field and 1.70/2.05 is none of the eight.
entries.replaced_by: eval/judge/field_ranks.py --rounds eval/runs/wg-tetris-judge-2026-08-17/pre (and /post). Quote value=rank order=pool, and name the field: 1.900 against 2.275 pre-repair, 2.100 against 1.925 post-repair.

entries.claim: finding #54 - `architecture` and `ux` share no evidence and rank the field identically on both presentation orders, so their agreement evidences a shared prior
entries.why: The claim rested on tau 1.00 across two presentation orders of ONE round, which is one observation reported twice. The repeat, with ux's evidence provably unchanged, gives tau 0.385 (seed 0, 13 comparable pairs) and 0.667 (seed 1, 12). The redundant pairs the second round does find are different ones and agree with neither.
entries.declared_in: eval/findings/certifies-nothing.md, finding #54, section 'WITHDRAWN 2026-08-17'; and eval/judge/JUDGING.md, 'RESULT after the repairs'
entries.replaced_by: What survives is the method, not the result: giving two judges disjoint evidence and checking they disagree is still the cheapest detector for a shared prior, but a positive reading needs repeats at a FIXED order (#58). Do not cite #54 as evidence of anything.

entries.claim: the deterministic tiers stated as '20 of 24 cells score exactly 1.000'
entries.why: It never said which 24 cells it counted. Eight different combinations of three 8-cell groups give exactly 20/24, and they disagree about which games and which runs are included - some spanning regime boundaries the docs elsewhere declare void. Summing across games is separately barred: the play-bot scores 13 criteria on pong and 22 on arena, so a 1.000 is a different achievement per column (#72).
entries.declared_in: README.md corrections table; tasks/05-state-the-criterion-count-disparity-as-its-o.md `established_by`; eval/IMPROVEMENTS.md, 'the test has fired five times'
entries.replaced_by: Per game, never summed. wg-matrix-2026-08-13: pong 5/8, tetris 5/8, arena 5/8. wg-audio48: pong 8/8, tetris 8/8. wg-g4c platformer: 6/8. Those counts are of stored `overall` under the pre-2026-08-23 weighted scheme and do not cross the tier-1-becomes-a-gate boundary recorded in eval/RUNS.md - state the scheme with the count.

entries.claim: the within-cell agreement stated as '0 verdict differences across 380 paired criteria'
entries.why: Both halves fail. The 2026-08-22 recount searched every coherent scope - all runs 1098 paired, wg-matrix alone 436, wg-matrix+wg-arena3d 584, wg-audio48 232, everything-except-g4 958, and by tier playbot 540 and programmatic 402 - and NONE gives 380. Six arbitrary subsets do, each mixing runs and games incoherently. And '0 verdict differences' is false in every scope with a plausible count: 5 for wg-matrix, 13 across all runs. Part of that drift is this project's own criterion repairs re-grading cells, so it may have been true when written - which is the argument for recording an aggregate's scope AND its date.
entries.replaced_by: Per scope, never pooled: wg-matrix (3 games) 436 paired criteria, 5 verdict differences, 332 differing evidence strings; wg-audio48 232 paired, 0 verdict differences, 120 differing evidence strings.

entries.claim: the within-cell evidence control stated as '219 of 380 evidence strings differ (58%)'
entries.why: It is the denominator of WR-paired-verdict-tie and dies with it: no coherent scope over the stored reports yields 380 paired criteria, so no scope yields 219 of them. The control it performs - showing the two trials in a cell are genuinely different artifacts - survives, but only per scope.
entries.replaced_by: Per scope: wg-matrix 332 of 436 differing evidence strings; wg-audio48 120 of 232. Quote the run with the ratio.
